A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cutoff rate of a MIMO system is a function of both the number of transmit and receive antennas, the normalized fade rate, the modulation scheme, and the channel-estimation method.
the effective cutoff rate is a useful tool for analyzing the finite-length performance of MIMO ST systems.

the effective cutoff rate is an appropriate metric to measure the performance of MIMO ST codes with finite codeword length and finite P f, especially for systems employing pilot-symbolassisted channel estimation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with finite codeword length, finite frame error probability, and imperfect CSIR, the cutoff rate is still a useful performance metric to characterize the performance of MIMO systems.

, for the finite-length MIMO ST codes, the cutoff rate is a more useful metric than the ergodic capacity, as the latter is only applicable to the asymptotic regime of infinite codeword length and zero frame error probability.
the cutoff rate is a very useful metric for the performance evaluation of MIMO systems.
